s: A company operates a fleet of servers on premises and operates a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in its organization in AWS Organizations. The company's AWS accounts contain hundreds of VPCs. The company wants to connect its AWS accounts to its on-premises network. AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections are already established to a single AWS account. The company wants to control which VPCs can communicate with other VPCs. Which combination of steps will achieve this level of control with the LEAST operational effort? (Choose three.)
o: Create a transit gateway in an AWS account. Share the transit gateway across accounts by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
Configure attachments to all VPCs and VPNs.
Set up transit gateway route tables. Associate the VPCs and VPNs with the route tables.
Configure VPC peering between the VPCs.
Configure attachments between the VPCs and VPNs.
Set up route tables on the VPCs and VPNs.
e: To connect on-premises network to hundreds of VPCs across multiple accounts with centralized control: l AWS Transit Gateway: Acts as a central hub for connecting VPCs and on-premises networks. Dramatically reduces operational complexity compared to managing individual VPN or peering connections l Transit Gateway attachments: Create attachments from Transit Gateway to each account's VPCs, allowing them to share the on-premises connectivity l Existing VPN integration: Connect the existing Site-to-Site VPN to Transit Gateway instead of a single VPC. Transit Gateway then distributes traffic to appropriate VPCs l Transit Gateway route tables: Use separate route tables to control which VPCs can communicate with other VPCs and on-premises networks. This provides the granular control requested while keeping operational effort minimal l Organization integration: Works with AWS Organizations for centralized management This approach scales to hundreds of VPCs with minimal operational overhead compared to managing individual connections.

w.y: Connecting hundreds of VPCs and VPNs with control over which VPCs talk to which is a transit gateway design. Share it with RAM, attach every VPC and VPN, and use multiple transit gateway route tables to segment traffic.

o.A: Correct: one transit gateway shared across accounts with AWS RAM.
o.B: Correct: attach all VPCs and VPNs to the transit gateway.
o.C: Correct: transit gateway route tables decide which attachments can reach each other.
o.D: Peering hundreds of VPCs is a mesh that does not scale and cannot carry VPN traffic transitively.
o.E: Attachments go from VPCs and VPNs to the transit gateway, not between VPCs and VPNs.
o.F: VPC route tables alone cannot segment traffic inside the transit gateway.
